questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following makes a person entitled to belong, live and to enjoy the full rights and privileges in a country?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Citizenship is the legal status that makes a person a full member of a country: it entitles him or her to live there and to enjoy all the rights and privileges that the law gives to citizens, and it also carries duties. A natural right belongs to every human being whatever the country, a legal right is one particular right written in law, and patriotism is only love and loyalty towards one's country. None of these three is the status that gives full membership.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A home characterized by conflicts, separation and divorce is referred to as a...
questions.corrige_markdown:
A home where the parents quarrel constantly, separate or divorce is called a broken home, because the family unit has been broken apart. The other expressions are not standard civic terms for a family in this situation.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A single - parent family is made up of ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
A single-parent family is a family in which only one parent (a father or a mother) lives with and brings up the children. Option A has one parent, the father, with his son and daughter, so it fits. Option C (father, mother and children) is a nuclear family with two parents. Option B has no children, and it adds relatives. Option D mentions step children, which describes a step or reconstituted family, so it is not the standard picture of a single-parent family.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: mother, step son and step daughter.

questions.enonce_markdown: According to the United Nations Convention on the Rights of a Child, the following are rights of children EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Convention on the Rights of the Child gives children, among others, the right to a name and nationality, the right to protection from harm and the right to rest and leisure. The right to vote is a political right of adult citizens, so it is not a right of children. The question asks for the exception.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A smaller part of a tribe made up of a group of families related through a common ancestor or marriage is called...
questions.corrige_markdown:
A clan is a part of a tribe formed by several families who are related through a common ancestor or through marriage. An ethnic group is larger than a clan (it is the whole community sharing language and culture), a village is a place where people live, and a quarter is a division of a town or village. Only the clan is defined by the family link.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The transitional light that permits pedestrians to cross the road with care is...

*Options as printed:* A) the orange light.   B) the green light.   C) the red light.   D) the yellow light.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Traffic lights have three colours: red means stop, green means go and the amber (orange) light is the transitional light between them. It warns that the signal is about to change, so pedestrians and drivers must act with care. The orange light is the usual name in Cameroon for the amber light.

**Intended answer: A (the orange light).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which one of the following is a road safety measure that must be respected by motorists on the carriage way in Cameroon?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In Cameroon vehicles drive on the right-hand side of the carriageway, so a motorist must keep to the right. Facing oncoming traffic is advice for a pedestrian who walks on a road without a pavement, not a rule for drivers. Avoiding the zebra crossing and parking on the pavement are offences, because drivers must give way to pedestrians at a zebra crossing and the pavement is reserved for pedestrians.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In technical schools, material for practical lessons is controlled by the...
questions.corrige_markdown:
In a technical school the Chief of Works is the officer in charge of the workshops and laboratories: he or she looks after the tools and materials used for practical lessons. The Vice Principal deals mainly with academic matters, the Senior Discipline Master with discipline, and the Principal manages the whole school.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Students are expected to take good care of the school environment by....

*Options as printed:* A) ensuring personal hygiene.   B) taking good care of the night watchman.   C) returning library books intact.   D) recycling domestic waste.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The school environment means the surroundings of the school: classrooms, compound, toilets and the waste produced there. Students take care of it by keeping it clean, putting waste in bins and recycling domestic waste where possible. Personal hygiene concerns the individual, caring for the night watchman concerns a person, and returning library books concerns school property. Because personal hygiene and the care of school property are also good habits in school, the printed question has no single clearly best answer.

**Intended answer: D (recycling domestic waste).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
One important duty of a traditional ruler as custodian of village land is to...

*Options as printed:* A) prevent the sale of land to foreigners.   B) preside over important festivals in the village.   C) issue land titles to villagers.   D) refer land disputes to the Divisional Officer.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Traditional rulers are auxiliaries of the administration. As custodians of the village land they help to keep peace over land matters, and when a land dispute cannot be settled in the village they refer it to the administrative authority, here the Divisional Officer. Land titles are issued by the State services, not by the chief, presiding over festivals has nothing to do with land, and the law does not give the chief a duty to forbid every sale of land to foreigners. The role of chiefs in land matters is described here in general terms, and the printed question is not precise enough to be marked automatically.

**Intended answer: D (refer land disputes to the Divisional Officer).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which is the most common reason for some of the inter-village conflicts in Cameroon?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Most conflicts between villages in Cameroon come from disputes over land: unclear boundaries, farmland, grazing land and inheritance of land. Quest for dominance, political influence and water sharing can also cause tension, but land disputes are the most common reason given in civic education.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which is the most appropriate reason for rural exodus?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Rural exodus is the movement of people, mostly young, from villages to towns. The main reason is the search for employment and a better income, because villages offer few jobs outside farming. Enjoying youthfulness is not a serious reason, health problems and electricity play a smaller part.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which human activity may most likely lead to environmental degradation?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Industrial expansion releases smoke, gases and liquid waste, and uses more raw materials, so it is the activity that most likely damages the environment. Solar energy and recycling protect the environment. Wind erosion is a natural process, not a human activity.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The following are consequences of environmental degradation, EXCEPT...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Environmental degradation leads to water scarcity, extreme weather (floods, droughts, storms) and the spread of diseases. Global warming, one of its effects, makes the sea level rise because ice melts, it does not make it fall. So fall in sea level is the exception.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In which of the following pairs of Regions in Cameroon do we find the Korup and Waza National Parks?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Korup National Park is a rain forest park in the South West Region and Waza National Park is a savannah park in the Far North Region. Option A is the only pair with these two Regions. In the other options the Region of one park is wrong.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: South West and Far North Regions

questions.enonce_markdown:
Who does the Divisional Officer represent in the subdivision?

*Options as printed:* A) Senior Divisional Officer   B) Minister of Territorial Administration and Decentralisation   C) Governor   D) President of the Republic
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Divisional Officer heads a subdivision and represents the central government there. In the usual civic education presentation the authorities of the territorial administration represent the Head of State and the Government, and through the hierarchy they report to the Senior Divisional Officer, the Governor and the Minister in charge of territorial administration. Several of the printed options can be defended and the name of the ministry given in option B is no longer the official one, so the printed question has no single safe key.

**Intended answer: D (President of the Republic).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which department in the Governor's office handles political issues and relates with the forces of Law and Order to maintain peace?

*Options as printed:* A) General Secretariat   B) Cabinet   C) Private Secretariat   D) Legal and Financial Affairs
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Governor is helped by several services. The General Secretariat coordinates the administrative services, the Private Secretariat handles the Governor's personal correspondence, and Legal and Financial Affairs deals with legal and financial files. The political and security matters, including the relations with the forces of law and order, are generally attributed to the Governor's Cabinet. The organisation of these offices has changed over time, so this reading is general and is not marked automatically.

**Intended answer: B (Cabinet).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The Coordination and control of the different administrative units is the function of which Ministry in Cameroon?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The administrative units (Regions, Divisions and Subdivisions headed by Governors, Senior Divisional Officers and Divisional Officers) are placed under the Ministry of Territorial Administration, which coordinates and controls them. The Ministry of Decentralisation and Local Development supervises the councils and regions as local authorities, the Ministry of Public Service deals with civil servants and the Ministry of Economic Planning with development planning.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Ministry of Public Service and Administrative Reforms
Ministry of Decentralisation and Local Government
Ministry of Economic Planning and Regional Development

questions.enonce_markdown: Bringing the administration closer to the people by the Cameroon government is called...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Decentralisation is the transfer of powers and resources from the central government to local authorities (councils and regions) so that decisions are taken closer to the people. Democracy is government by the people, regional balance concerns sharing of posts and development between regions, and national integration is about unity among the people.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: If Mr. Ayuk awards a public contract to Mr. Kum simply because they were classmates in the primary school, Mr. Ayuk is guilty of...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Nepotism is giving jobs, contracts or other advantages to relatives or close friends instead of choosing on merit. Here the contract is given because of a personal link of friendship (classmates), so the closest term is nepotism. Bigotry is intolerance of other beliefs, fraud is dishonest deception for gain, and tribalism is favouring people of one's own tribe, which is not mentioned. The link is a school friendship, not a family link, so the word is used here in its broad sense of favouritism.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Vanessa is 14 years old and in Form 4. She left the house for school, but branched to her boyfriend's room and stayed there till closing time. Vanessa is guilty of...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Juvenile delinquency means wrong or anti-social behaviour by young people under the age of adulthood. A pupil who leaves home for school but goes elsewhere (truancy) is behaving in a delinquent way. Nothing in the story says she was paid for sex, so prostitution is wrong. Peer pressure is a cause, not an offence, and she has not left school for good, so it is not school dropout.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The devaluation of the CFA Franc in 1993 drove many civil servants into the habit of collecting extra charges for services rendered to citizens. This shows the direct relationship between...
questions.corrige_markdown:
After the devaluation and the salary cuts of the early 1990s the buying power of civil servants fell. Many of them asked citizens for extra payments for services that should be free or fixed by law, which is corruption. This links low wages and corruption. Tribalism and unemployment are not mentioned in the statement, and embezzlement is the theft of public funds, not the collection of extra charges from users.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which one of the following is both a cause and an effect of prostitution?

*Options as printed:* A) Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs).   B) Unemployment.   C) Unwanted pregnancies.   D) Divorce.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Prostitution is the sale of sexual services. Among the causes usually listed are poverty, unemployment, peer pressure and broken homes. Among the effects are STIs, unwanted pregnancies, divorce and social shame. Divorce and unemployment can each be defended as both a cause and an effect, so the printed question has no single clearly best answer.

**Intended answer: D (Divorce).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The programme launched by the Cameroon government to fish out illegally employed citizens in the country is known as...

*Options as printed:* A) Operation Sparrow Hawk.   B) Operation Epervier.   C) Operation Antilope.   D) Operation Green Revolution.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Operation Sparrow Hawk is the English name of Operation Epervier, so options A and B name the same operation, which is the campaign against the embezzlement of public funds. The operation aimed at cleaning the civil service of irregularly recruited staff is generally given as Operation Antilope. Because two options are the same and the facts cannot be checked from the printed paper, this question is not marked automatically.

**Intended answer: C (Operation Antilope).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following is a preventive measure taken by the Cameroon government against drug abuse?

*Options as printed:* A) Creation of treatment centres for drug addicts.   B) Fixing of minimum age for prescription of drugs.   C) Banning the importation of alcohol.   D) Intensification of the fight against poverty.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A preventive measure acts before the problem appears. Treatment centres are curative, because they care for people who are already addicted. Fixing a minimum age for the prescription of drugs restricts access for the young and is the only option that is clearly preventive in nature. The claim that Cameroon bans the importation of alcohol is not accurate, and the fight against poverty is only an indirect measure. The facts in the options cannot be checked from the printed paper, so the question is not marked automatically.

**Intended answer: B (Fixing of minimum age for prescription of drugs).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The best form of government has been acclaimed to be democracy because...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Democracy is acclaimed because power belongs to the people: rulers are chosen by the majority of voters and decisions follow the will of the majority, while the rights of the minority are respected. It does not eliminate social ills, an elected minority would not be democratic, and in practice not all citizens take part in elections.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: it is the government by elected majority.
it is the government by elected minority.

questions.enonce_markdown:
How many of Cameroon's national symbols carry 'Peace-Work-Fatherland' on them?

*Options as printed:* A) 1   B) 2   C) 3   D) 4
questions.corrige_markdown:
'Peace - Work - Fatherland' is the national motto of Cameroon. In the usual civic education teaching it is written on the coat of arms, so the number of symbols is one. The flag carries the star and the colours, and the anthem is a song. Other official emblems may also repeat the motto, so the printed question is not precise enough to be marked automatically.

**Intended answer: A (1).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which Constitution moved Cameroon from a Federal Republic to a United Republic?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The 1961 Constitution created the Federal Republic of Cameroon. The 1972 Constitution, adopted after a referendum, abolished the federal structure and created the United Republic of Cameroon. The 1984 change only altered the name to Republic of Cameroon, and the 1996 Constitution introduced decentralisation, among other changes.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: From the list below, identify an important change that was adopted in the 1996 Constitution.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The 1996 revision of the Constitution made decentralisation a feature of the State by providing for Regions and local councils as decentralised authorities, and it also provided for a Senate. The post of Prime Minister already existed before 1996, the name of the country changed in 1984, and the anthem was not modified by the Constitution.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: The post of Prime Minister was created
The Cameroon National Anthem was modified
The name of the country was changed
There was the introduction of decentralisation.

questions.enonce_markdown: The legislative arm of government in Cameroon is bi-cameral. This means that...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Bi-cameral means 'two chambers'. The legislature of Cameroon has two houses: the National Assembly (lower house) and the Senate (upper house). The meaning has nothing to do with the sex of members, with the way laws are made or with the languages spoken.

**Answer: A.**
themes: separation of powers and arms of government

choix.texte: it has both lower and upper houses.
it has both men and women as members.
it makes and adopts laws at once.
members speak both English and French.

questions.enonce_markdown:
One important responsibility of a member of parliament towards citizens is to...

*Options as printed:* A) respect party discipline.   B) attend all parliamentary sessions.   C) complain in case of marginalisation.   D) represent the state in his/her constituency.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A member of parliament is elected by citizens to speak and vote for them, to make laws and to control the government. His duties towards the voters include attending the sessions of Parliament so that their interests are defended. Respecting party discipline is a duty towards the party. Several printed options can be defended (representing the constituency, voicing the complaints of the people) and the wording 'represent the state' is not exact, so the printed question has no single clearly best answer.

**Intended answer: B (attend all parliamentary sessions).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following requires the participation of all the three arms of government?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The three arms of government are the legislature (makes laws), the executive (applies them and promulgates them) and the judiciary (interprets and applies them in court). Adopting a law is done by Parliament, promulgating it is done by the Head of State, and interpreting it is done by the courts, so all three arms take part. Control of government action is done by Parliament, and election disputes by the courts. The appointment of members of the Constitutional Council is shared among several authorities, but the option that clearly shows the three arms in the textbook is D.

**Answer: D.**
themes: separation of powers and arms of government

choix.texte: Control of government action by parliamentarians.
Appointment of members of the Constitutional Council.
Handling of election irregularities by the Supreme Court.
Adoption, promulgation and interpretation of laws.

questions.enonce_markdown:
In the electoral process, the practice of universal adult suffrage involves...

*Options as printed:* A) all male adults.   B) female and male adults.   C) the right to vote for everyone.   D) the right to vote for males only.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Universal adult suffrage means that all adult citizens, men and women alike, have the right to vote, without discrimination of sex, wealth, tribe or religion. Options A and D leave out women. Option B states the idea exactly, and option C also expresses it loosely, although 'everyone' would include children, so the printed question has no single clearly best answer.

**Intended answer: B (female and male adults).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: A situation in the country where the electorate is asked to either accept or reject a proposal on an issue of national importance is referred to as...
questions.corrige_markdown:
In a referendum all registered voters are asked to say yes or no to a proposal, such as a change to the constitution or a major national policy. Democracy is a system of government, freedom of expression is a right, and a plebiscite is a vote of the people on a question of status, such as the 1961 vote on the future of Southern Cameroons. In ordinary civic education the definition given in the question is the definition of a referendum.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The following are electoral malpractices in Cameroon except...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Electoral malpractices are acts that break the electoral law or make the vote unfair: voting more than once (multiple voting), campaigning on the day of the vote, when campaigning is closed, and counting the same ballots twice. Rejecting null ballots, that is ballot papers that are not validly filled, is a normal and legal part of counting. It is therefore the exception.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Trade by Barter simply means the...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Barter is trade without money: one good or service is exchanged directly for another. An exchange of a mirror for cowries is only one example, and cowries were a form of money in some places. Exchange of human beings is the slave trade, and palm oil for pounds uses money. The general meaning is the exchange of goods for goods.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: exchange of human beings for finished goods.
exchange of palm oil for pounds.

questions.enonce_markdown: The main aim of social security in Cameroon is to...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Social security is a system, run in Cameroon by the National Social Insurance Fund, that protects workers and their families against risks: old age through pensions, work accidents and occupational diseases, and family allowances including maternity. Its aim is therefore the welfare of employees. It does not control road accidents, create jobs or give aid after disasters.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: limit the rate of highway accidents.
cater for the welfare of employees.

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify a condition that is not necessary for economic growth to lead to economic development.
questions.corrige_markdown:
For growth to become development, a country needs political will, a trained and educated population and good management of resources. Capital flight, the movement of money out of the country, deprives the country of funds to invest, so it is not a condition for development: it works against it. Population expansion is a factor that can help or hinder development depending on how it is managed, and the printed wording is ambiguous.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is not a source of government revenue?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Government revenue is the money that comes in: taxes and customs duties, loans from other countries and the sale of bonds. Paying salaries to civil servants is money going out, so it is government expenditure, not revenue.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Payment of salaries to civil servants

questions.enonce_markdown: Tax evasion is detrimental to the entire community because it leads to...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Tax evasion means deliberately not paying the taxes due. The State then has less revenue to build schools, hospitals and roads, so public investment falls and the whole community suffers. Evasion does not reduce the burden for honest taxpayers, who may have to pay more, and it does not directly lower consumption of necessities.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: No one, not even the State, can take away your inalienable rights because they are ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Inalienable rights, such as the right to life, belong to every person because he or she is a human being: they are natural rights. They are not granted by the State, so the State cannot take them away. The other options describe wrong sources of the rights.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: "Carries out investigations on the violation of human rights and reports to the government" This is the duty of the ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
The National Commission on Human Rights and Freedoms is the Cameroonian body that investigates reports of violations of human rights and reports to the authorities. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights is a text, not a body that investigates. The International Court of Justice settles disputes between States and the International Criminal Court tries individuals for the gravest crimes.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: National Commission on Human Rights and Freedoms.

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the date when the Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted by the UN General Assembly.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly on 10 December 1948. This date is celebrated every year as Human Rights Day. The year 1945 is the foundation of the United Nations.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: After a quarrel between your father and mother, they went to sleep in different rooms. You were so worried that you decided to visit each of them to find out the cause of the disagreement in order to arrive at a solution. This action of yours can be described as...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Going to each parent to understand the cause of the quarrel and to bring them back together is an effort to restore good relations, which is reconciliation. An armistice is an agreement to stop fighting between warring parties, a compromise is when each side gives up something, and collaboration is working together. Mediation would also describe the action, but it is not offered, so reconciliation is the best choice.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The principal role of the Red Cross is...
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Red Cross is a humanitarian movement. Its main role is to help and care for people in trouble: the wounded, victims of wars and disasters, refugees, and to give first aid and relief. It is not a police force against crime, it does not prevent wars, and promoting human rights is the work of other bodies.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: to care for those in trouble.

questions.enonce_markdown: An outstanding effect of conflict which retards a nation's progress and development is the...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Conflict makes investors leave and businesses close, so there is loss of investments and the economy stops growing, which delays progress and development. Outburst of violence and crackdown on demonstrators are the conflict itself or the reaction to it, rather than an effect that slows development.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Ideas or beliefs mostly about women which are bias and very often wrong, but are generally accepted, are known as...
questions.corrige_markdown:
A stereotype is a fixed and oversimplified belief about a group that is accepted by many people. When it concerns men or women it is a gender stereotype, such as the idea that girls cannot study science. Gender violence is harmful action, marginalization is leaving people out, and inequality is unequal treatment.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following is most likely to hinder the education of the girl child?

*Options as printed:* A) Early pregnancy   B) Poverty   C) Peer pressure   D) High cost of Education
questions.corrige_markdown:
Several factors keep girls out of school: early marriage and pregnancy, poverty and the high cost of schooling, and peer pressure. Early pregnancy usually forces a girl to leave school and is specific to girls, but poverty and high cost of education also affect many girls, so the printed question has no single clearly best answer.

**Intended answer: A (Early pregnancy).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: One undesirable effect of globalization is...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Globalization increases links between countries. Its positive effects include higher output and the spread of education. Brain drain, the departure of skilled people from poorer countries to richer ones, is a harmful effect because the home country loses the skills it trained. The spread of multinationals is a feature that has good and bad sides.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A Form 2 student of 11 years old is sent home for fees and the parents ask him to hawk boiled groundnuts for 2 weeks, in order to raise the fees. This is an example of...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Child labour is the use of children in work that suits neither their age nor their schooling and that harms their education or health. A child of 11 sent to hawk goods for two weeks to raise fees is a clear case. Child trafficking involves moving children to be exploited, which is not described, and parental neglect means failing to look after the child. Exploitation is a wider term, so the most precise answer is child labour.

**Answer: D.**
